answer: A single kernel checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called an ocean, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 486 aliases therefore costs 448 bonds held for 8 days each, plus the sparrow attestations those aliases can never earn. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
